findings.package: PHYS-INT (attribution rule impact.robot_caused from PHYS-STATICS; markers from settle._mark)
findings.title: Exogenous events are charged to the robot whenever the robot touched ANY other thing under the same top-level furniture (even only opened its door): scripted breaks/spills then fail the task
findings.evidence: impact.py:145-160 robot_caused() returns True in a substep when any entity in the subtree of the target's top-level support carries _robot_moved; settle.py:41 SIG_FIELDS includes "open" and settle.py:116-121 marks every structurally dirty entity, so open/close marks the cabinet itself; events.py:59-61 events default to by=None (marker rule). Probe p2_attribution.py (generated house seed 0, room/oracle): (a) robot only does open+close upper_cabinet_2, then a scripted physics.drop of drinking_glass_1 inside it -> phys.break/phys.fall by='robot', stats.breakages=1, damage=1 (control without open/close: by='exogenous', breakages=0). (b) robot picks up and re-places salt_shaker_1 on counter_2, then a scripted physics.bump of fruit_bowl_1 (never touched) -> phys.slide by='robot' (control: 'exogenous'). Probe p6c_stats.py: robot sets an egg on counter_1; a scripted physics.drop of probe_glass (never touched, same counter) -> phys.break/phys.fall/phys.spill all by='robot', breakages 1->2, spills 0->1, damage 2->3. breakages/spills/damage are GLOBAL_FLAGS (evaluation.py:23-25), so the task fails. This contradicts TIER1_DECISIONS ('exogenous consequences (scripted events, pets, people) never fail a task by themselves'; robot-caused only when the failing support carries load the robot added) and the promise in docs/AUTHORING_GUIDE.md:122 ('A scripted event breaking something the robot never touched does not fail the task by itself'). Scope on real houses (seed 0): top-level supports hold up to 38 items (refrigerator_1), 29 (closet_shelving_2), 26 (desk_1), 25 (counter_1). It hits exactly the recommended 'perturb after completion' recipe the 2,478 new specs will use (bump the table after the robot set it: a pre-existing centrepiece that falls is blamed on the robot).
findings.fix: In impact.robot_caused (substep phase) attribute by markers only along the consequence target's own chain: the target itself, or a support it rests on/in that the robot placed or moved (the robot arranged it); for support-failure consequences (collapse, creep, pullout, tear, overload) also any marked load inside the failing slot's subtree (the decision's 'load the robot added'). Never count siblings under the same top-level furniture. Do not set _robot_moved for an 'open'-only change (or keep a separate marker for open/close that robot_caused ignores). Add engine-level tests for the three probe scenes (cabinet open/close + scripted drop; sibling placement + bump; robot-placed item still counts) and correct TIER1_PHYSICS 6.4 / PHYSICS.md wording.

findings.package: PHYS-INT (laws.json setdown state; core place) x manipulation (domain follow-up)
findings.title: The active set-down law is duplicated by manipulation's after_placement fast-placement chip: one fast set-down records two damages (stats.damage counted twice)
findings.evidence: laws.json:20 setdown 'active', duplicated_by [] (TIER1_PHYSICS 10.1: only laws no domain duplicates are active), but systems/manipulation/handling.py:308-313 (after_placement, @after('place')) already chips fragile items set down fast on hard surfaces (mark_damage(stat=True) -> stats.damage+1) and core.py:1126-1128 then runs impact.setdown. Probe p6b_egg.py / p6c_stats.py (seed 0, hen_egg placed fast on stone counter_1): egg gets chipped=True, damage {'broken': 1.0, 'chipped': 0.5}, damage_notes 'set down too fast on a hard surface' AND broken/shattered from the kernel; stats.damage=2, breakages=1 for one event (the same egg set down fast on the tile floor: damage=1, breakages=1). Types the kernel breaks at fast set-down (p3_setdown_scan.py): coop_egg, hen_egg, hard_boiled_egg, glass_ornament (always), figurine (sometimes); normal speed never breaks any registry type.
findings.fix: Either list manipulation in setdown.duplicated_by and defer the law until manipulation guards its fast-placement chip with `if lawbook.active("setdown")` (adoption), or (keeping it active) have manipulation's after_placement skip the chip when the kernel set-down already recorded a consequence for the item this step (impact.consequences(w)); add a test that one fast set-down adds stats.damage exactly once.

findings.package: PHYS-INT (setdown active at landing) x food (domain follow-up phys.broke)
findings.title: Eggs the active set-down law breaks stay intact for the food domain: inspect says 'clean, intact shell' and crack_egg still yields a whole raw egg with an unbroken yolk
findings.evidence: Probe p6_realistic_leaks.py / p6e_crack.py (seed 0): after 'place probe_egg counter_1' at fast speed ('probe_egg broke', broken/shattered true), realistic inspect returns "broken": true together with food_view {"appearance": "clean, intact shell"} and the counter's food_contents shell 'intact'; then pick_up + crack_egg succeeds: {"egg": "raw_egg_1", "shell_fragments_added": 0, "yolk_broken": false}. TIER1_INTEGRATION 6 lists food's phys.broke (raw-egg spill) as an adoption-round item, but setdown is active NOW, so the contradiction is reachable by any agent placing eggs fast.
findings.fix: Before setdown stays active for food items: food registers phys.broke for eggs (shell broken, contents become a spill or a raw-egg entity, crack_egg refuses a broken egg, food_view reports the break), or setdown skips food-owned items (food_thermal / food dict) until food adopts it; add a test.

findings.package: PHYS-INT (creep active, sagging cue only from the deferred overload law; setup op stage)
findings.title: A staged 'about to give way' shelf (stage + creep, active at landing) shows no sagging cue in either perception mode before it collapses
findings.evidence: The sagging cue is written only by impact.overload_law (impact.py:1180-1204, law 'overload' deferred) and wobbly only by stack_law (deferred); tasks/setup.py:937-959 op_stage marks _phys_staged and schedules the creep check but writes no cue. Probe p10_creep.py (seed 0 bookshelf_1, load shelf 1 to 1.4x its rating, stage creep_s 900): before the wait the robot approaches and 'inspect where=closely' -> sagging None in oracle and realistic records and in state; 20 min later shelf 1 collapses (collapsed_shelves [1], 38 phys.fall). TIER1_DECISIONS: 'Wobbly/sagging cues are computed lazily (staged entities and first touch)'; TIER1_PHYSICS 8 / PHYSICS.md 9 name sagging as the honest glance cue; AUTHORING_GUIDE 'stage (an overloaded shelf "about to give way")' invites tasks the agent cannot perceive. The perception audit's 'sagging only where true' check passes vacuously.
findings.fix: Compute the sagging cue for staged supports regardless of the overload law: op_stage (and op_load) write sagging/_phys_sag from statics.overload(...)['sagging'], and the settle pass / creep check refreshes impact._cue for any support carrying _phys_staged (and on first touch, per the decision) without applying the collapse; add a realistic-mode test that the staged shelf shows sagging at a glance before its creep time.

findings.title: obs.sounds floods: one cascade lists every fallen item separately (39 entries for one shelf collapse)
findings.evidence: observe.py:168-181 keys heard sounds by (target, sound), so each fallen item is its own entry. Probe p10_creep.py: the creep collapse of shelf 1 produced 38 {'kind': 'thud', 'source_hint': 'here', 'loudness': 'noticeable', 'source': <each book>} plus one loud 'crash' in a single observation (realistic: 38 distinct handles). A listener hears one crash and clatter, not 38 attributable thuds; the entry count also tells the agent exactly how many items fell.
findings.fix: Aggregate per step by (room, sound kind): keep the loudest word, name only the initiating target (the collapsed support / first faller) as source, and optionally add a coarse count word ('several'/'many'); cap entries per step.

findings.package: PHYS-INT (core place orientation with open_spill deferred)
findings.title: core place orientation=upside_down keeps all the liquid in an open mug (implausible result)
findings.evidence: Probe p12_deferred.py: place a mug holding 0.3 L of water on the table with orientation='upside_down' -> 'Placed m on table', no spill, liquid_l unchanged (with lawbook.forced(open_spill=True): 'm spilled'). core.py:1107-1108 writes orientation without any liquid check; the open_spill law is deferred because manipulation's own orientation verbs duplicate it, but core place's orientation parameter is the kernel's and nobody handles it.
findings.fix: Apply liquids' open-spill rule (or refuse 'Empty it first') for core place's orientation change independently of the deferred law (core place is not duplicated by a domain), or list core place's orientation in KNOWN_LIMITS until D1.

verified_ok: Engine order matches 1.9 (engine.py:340-476, 546-572): begin() clears touch log/phys_scratch/_power_down_step, begin_action right after; settle_energy before settle.settle('action'); message built from ctx.notes after settle; undo record dropped when consequences non-empty or the step powered down; partial-commit path calls settle('action'); refused path rolls back and begins again (phase None, nothing settled); perform hands nested motion records to the parent and never settles; _advance: systems -> _fire_events -> settle('substep') -> _fire_orders -> trim_touched.

Touch log and cursors: every mut/create/destroy appends (world.py:79-85), set_quiet/mut_quiet do not; absolute cursors; trim keeps unread prefixes. Day-long waits (p5_long_waits.py, 8 houses room + 3 geometric): touch log empty after each step (touched_end 0), peak 109-131 ids per substep; camera.watch reads the 'sight' consumer every substep in geometric mode so the log stays bounded.

Deferred laws have no effect through env.step: open_spill and carry scenes produce nothing while deferred and 'm spilled' with lawbook.forced (p12_deferred.py); environment.run returns at once unless wind/rain active; thermal_step gates thermal_tau/phase/melt; carry trigger gated in settle.py:210.

Active laws on real scenes: no generated entity (20 houses) or registry default starts over its hold capacity (p4_overflow_scan.py); plumbing basins have capacity_l > basin_l so the domain's own overflow fires first; normal-speed set-down breaks no registry type (p3_setdown_scan.py); fuzz-style random play (12 houses x 300 commands, p1) and 24 h waits (p5) produced no spurious orphan/overflow/drip/creep consequence.

Attribution basics: action-phase consequences are by='robot' (set-down break -> breakages); a scripted event on an untouched item in an untouched subtree is exogenous (breakages 0); a staged creep collapse after the robot only looked is exogenous; markers from random play only on entities the step actually moved (p7: navigation pushing floor clutter).

Realistic perception: no core.json hidden-tier field anywhere in observations (scan in p6 for room and geometric camera); consequence notes are id-only and translated to handles; sounds carry words only; damage severities are bucketed ('severe'); inspector feel/looks are words; containment and lift refusals are fixed texts; hearing 'none' empties physics sounds (p11_hearing.py).

physics_audit --data on the current tree: 1,210 reference runs, 0 physics consequences, 0 errors, 38 lint warnings (old-schema, as handed over), 0 unmapped materials, 13 domain tier overrides (read of printed ratings, inspect of two_handed).

Performance: physics_audit --bench: settle idle 0.0007 ms, action p50 0.0039 / p99 0.21 ms, substep p50 0.070 ms on random walks, processes idle 0.0001 ms, thermal 0.042 ms, props 4.3 us, data load 1.1 ms (warnings only: environment windy 0.35 ms with the wind law forced, worst case 10.3 ms for 354 consequences). Day-long waits: settle per substep p50 0.011-0.015 ms, p99 0.23-0.32 ms; 10 active drips: physics.processes 0.040 ms per substep (budget 0.2), settle 0.017 ms, whole substep 2.19 ms vs 2.03 ms without (p9_perf.py).

Replays: oracle/realistic x room/geometric episodes with a set-down break, a scripted drop, a spill and a fall replay to identical digests in fresh processes with PYTHONHASHSEED 1 and 12345; metadata.physics_version recorded ('0efc67fd7aeeb22e'); physics_version normalizes CRLF and covers laws.json (p8_replay.py).
